name: System X
goal: Scene generation, iterative multimodal VR editing, post-session preference memory construction, and retrieval policy optimization across authoring sessions.
description: the system generates indoor VR environments that users modify through speech and controller interactions. It learns reusable spatial preferences from completed scenes and adapts subsequent scene generation through preference retrieval and reinforcement learning. Actors: model_1 = automatic speech recognition model; model_2 = large language model; model_3 = text embedding model; model_4 = cross-attention scene retrieval reranker; model_5 = cross-attention affordance retrieval reranker; model_6 = large language model; model_7 = vision-language model; tool_1 = constraint-based 3D indoor scene generation engine; tool_2 = VR runtime and scene editing system; tool_3 = preference retrieval and sampling pipeline; tool_4 = spatial context extraction and constraint grounding pipeline; tool_5 = policy-gradient optimizer with LoRA.

processes.name: Generate personalized VR scene
processes.description: When the user requests an indoor scene, a model_3 embedding model retrieves relevant historical scenes, and two cross-attention rerankers select scene memories and spatial affordances. tool_1 combines the retrieved preferences with room constraints to generate an indoor layout, which tool_2 presents in VR. The user can generate another scene with a new request and updated preference memory.

processes.name: Edit VR scene through speech and controllers
processes.description: After a scene is generated, the user selects objects and target positions with VR controllers and speaks editing commands. model_1 transcribes the speech, an LLM resolves spatial references and decomposes the request into atomic operations, and tool_2 executes the edits. This repeats until the user finishes editing the scene.

processes.name: Learn spatial preferences and update retrieval policy
processes.description: After editing ends, the system analyzes the final scene and interaction history to identify functional object groups, local spatial relationships, and global room connectivity. An LLM infers design preferences and affordances, which are converted into symbolic spatial constraints and stored in persistent memory. A vision-language model evaluates whether previously retrieved affordances appear in the final scene, and the resulting rewards update the retrieval rerankers for future sessions.

representations.request: the user's text request for an indoor scene
representations.preference_memory: stored spatial preferences and past scenes from earlier sessions
representations.retrieval_policy: the learned settings that decide which memories are retrieved
representations.candidate_scenes: past scenes similar to the request
representations.scored_scenes: relevance scores for the candidate scenes
representations.sampled_scenes: the past scenes chosen to guide generation
representations.scored_affordances: relevance scores for stored spatial preferences
representations.sampled_affordances: the spatial preferences chosen to guide generation
representations.room_constraints: the size and layout limits of the room
representations.retrieval_trace: a record of which memories and preferences were used
representations.generation_constraints: the combined constraints passed to the layout generator
representations.scene_graph: the generated layout: objects and their spatial relations
representations.interaction_log: a record of the user's edits in VR
representations.targets: objects and positions the user points at with the controllers
representations.transcript: the text of the spoken command
representations.interaction_state: the command combined with what the user pointed at
representations.resolved_instruction: the command with references like 'this' and 'there' resolved to objects and positions
representations.edit_subtasks: the command split into simple edit operations
representations.session_payload: the final scene and edit history packaged for analysis
representations.object_features: per-object properties such as type, size and position
representations.functional_zones: groups of objects that serve one function, such as a reading corner
representations.geometric_context: spatial relations between objects and the room layout
representations.hierarchical_context: the scene described from room to zones to objects
representations.affordances: inferred design preferences, written as short statements
representations.spatial_constraints: the preferences turned into rules a layout generator can use
representations.topdown_view: a top-down image of the final scene
representations.realization_signals: whether each retrieved preference appears in the final scene
representations.rewards: scores used to update the retrieval settings
